script.flip1: Surviving flip for the pass overs: game stays competitive or ATL leads, GB never exits the pass game, and Watson/Golden keep the 9-plus target shares seen in weeks 1-2.
script.flip2: Kill flip: GB gets up big early and clocks it with Lloyd/Brooks/Johnson, so Watson and Golden yards stall late (same shape as a favorite-runs-the-clock script). Both overs are tagged script-dependent on that flip.

matchup.bleeds: ATL bleeds explosives (8 passes of 20+ on 81 att) and, on a tiny sample, the middle (14.12 YPA, 8 att). Outside is not soft (5.14/6.36). ATL run D is fine (3.41 YPC, 2 runs of 10+). GB is the stingy side: 3.05 YPC, 3 runs of 10+, only 2 passes of 20+ on 72 att.
matchup.overlap: GB's top options are the air-yard WRs, Watson 213 air and Golden 217 air, which overlaps ATL's explosive-play leak, not a proven outside-YPA leak. Cannot map them to the middle — no target-location charting. ATL's primary, Bi.Robinson, runs into GB's strength (3.05 YPC), so he is not an over.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Christian Watson beats 71.5 receiving yards because he is GB's downfield WR1 at 9.5 targets, 94 yards and 106.5 air yards per game, and ATL has already allowed 8 passes of 20+ while blitzing only 21%, the pocket where Love's EPA is positive.
edge_players.must_be_true: Tagged script-dependent. Watson keeps the week 1-2 WR1 target/air share, Love stays pass-lean for most of the game, and he is full-go (health not in pack).
edge_players.kills_it: GB jumps ahead and grinds with Lloyd/Brooks/Johnson, or ATL brackets him and the 2-game 94-yard rate regresses through the 71.5 cushion; outside YPA allowed (5.14 left, 6.36 right) says this is not a soft corner matchup on paper.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Matthew Golden beats 55.5 receiving yards because he has the same downfield role as Watson (9 targets, 76.5 yards, 108.5 air yards per game) against the defense that has allowed the explosives, and 55.5 sits about 21 yards under that rate.
edge_players.must_be_true: Tagged script-dependent. Golden keeps a co-primary share beside Watson rather than ceding targets to Reed/Kraft/Moore, and GB does not exit the pass game early.
edge_players.kills_it: Target split with Watson in a shorter game, or the same blowout clock-kill; one of the two air-yard WRs can miss even if GB passes.

market_rung_price: christianwatson recyds over 71.5 -112; matthewgolden recyds over 55.5 -113. Main-board rungs near even, not short-priced alts. No passing yards, TDs, or receptions.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost because the weeks 1-2 GB passing lines were opponent-driven, ATL's eight explosives were noise while the real splits (outside 5.14 and 6.36 YPA) held, Love saw more pressure than a 21% blitz rate implies (blitz EPA -0.24; pressure rate not in the pack), and GB led and handed it to the Lloyd/Brooks/Johnson committee so Watson and Golden split a short target pie and both finished under 71.5 and 55.5. No spread was saved, so the market may already have priced a lower-pass script this read invented from two games.
slip_story: One story only: GB downfield pass stack (Watson over 71.5 with Golden over 55.5) in a pass-lean script against an explosives-allowing, low-blitz ATL defense. They win together if GB throws all game and lose together if GB runs the clock. Do not mix with a game under or with ATL skill-position overs. Not a GB-runs-the-clock stack and not a Bijan rush-under stack.
